transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm just having some issues with my work lately. I'm an auditor, and... well, I keep starting these follow-up items after audits, or sometimes mentorship events. I have every intention of finishing them. But then... I don't know, days later I'll find out that the final email, or a review note, or a form just... never actually got done. So, I figured I should probably make an appointment.
Have you noticed these kinds of difficulties with finishing tasks throughout your life, or is this something that started more recently?

Um... I suppose it's not really a new thing. It's kind of always been there. 

Like, even back in elementary school... my report cards usually said I was bright, but... I don't know, that I lost assignments, or rushed past small details. Talked out of turn. I guess I always needed reminders to actually finish my work. My mother actually still jokes about it sometimes... she says I could ace a test but completely forget about the project sitting right in my backpack. 

So... yeah. It's not recent.
As an adult, do you often feel restless inside or find it hard to sit still for long periods?

Um... yes, I suppose so. 

Sitting still for a long review... it's just, it feels physically uncomfortable. It's like this pressure building up inside me. Eventually, I just... I need to stand up. I'll walk to the printer, or just find some reason to move around. It's hard to just stay in the chair.
Do you often find yourself interrupting people or finishing their sentences before they're done speaking?

Um... yeah. I suppose so. 

I do catch myself jumping into conversations before people finish... especially with the junior auditors. It's just... I don't know, the answer feels really urgent in my head, I guess. So I end up blurting it out before I can really stop myself.
